## Professional Summary

Carlos C. Goller is a Teaching Professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at North Carolina State University. His work brings together microbiology, biotechnology, genomics, open education, and inquiry-driven teaching, with a focus on building accessible, research-rich learning experiences for students.

## Teaching and Curriculum Leadership

Goller's teaching emphasizes discovery, collaboration, and communication, encouraging students to learn science through authentic inquiry and the creation of shared knowledge.

### Selected Courses

- **MB 360 — Microbiology**, North Carolina State University
- **LSC 170 — Microbial Superheroes**, North Carolina State University
- **HON 312 — Outbreak**, North Carolina State University Honors Program
- **BIT 477/577 — Metagenomics**, NC State Biotechnology Program
- **BIT 479/579 — High-throughput Discovery**, NC State Biotechnology Program
- **BIT 495/595 — Portable Genome Sequencing**, NC State Biotechnology Program
- **BIT 495/595 — Metabolic Modeling**, NC State Biotechnology Program
- **BIT 295 — Biotechnology and Sustainability**, NC State Biotechnology Program
- **OPEN 9200 — Open Education Resources and Pedagogies**, Kwantlen Polytechnic University

### Curriculum Development Themes

- Inquiry-driven laboratory design in microbiology and biotechnology
- Integration of genomics, bioinformatics, and high-throughput discovery into teaching
- Open pedagogy and open educational resource development
- Technology-enhanced instruction, including electronic lab notebooks and collaborative annotation

## Research and Scholarship

### Research Areas

- Microbial pathogenesis and antimicrobial strategy development
- Molecular epidemiology of clinically relevant microorganisms
- Undergraduate-centered discovery projects in microbiology and genomics
- Environmental and applied microbiology
- Open education, biotechnology education, and curriculum development

### Scholarship Highlights

- Publications span microbiology, biotechnology education, bioinformatics education, open pedagogy, and course-based undergraduate research.
- Scholarship includes peer-reviewed journal articles, book chapters, educational resources, and collaborative teaching publications.
- Full publication records are maintained on the [Publications](publications.qmd) page.

## Mentoring

Goller has mentored undergraduate researchers, graduate students, and postdoctoral education scholars across microbiology, biotechnology, education, and related interdisciplinary fields.

- Full mentoring records are maintained on the [Mentoring](mentoring.qmd) page.
